coverage.evidence: 'Every reference to a Peer AI version names 1.0.0-next.18 and none names next.16.' Searched every json, yml, md and js file outside node_modules. Four references, all next.18: .mcp.json's MCP command, .claude/settings.json's render hook, .github/workflows/peer-ai.yml's check step, and package.json's peer-ai-eslint-config pin. The remaining next.16 strings are prose describing history rather than versions in use - two deferral reasons in peer-ai.config.json recording which release fixed the max-lines bug, this item's own title and goal, and CONTEXT.md's dated entries - and the lockfile resolves all three Peer AI packages at next.18.

'Anything the project does not need is identified and decided rather than committed unread.' render added no workflow at all: the diff under .github/workflows is peer-ai.yml only, gaining the draft condition, the ready_for_review trigger and the version. The security pipeline and the digest-pinned OWASP ZAP image in next.18's notes apply to projects with a server, and this product has none - recorded in the pull request body and in the infrastructure review's SEC-23 and OPS-01 lines rather than left as an assumption. The full text of both workflow files was read before committing.

'doctor and check pass on next.18 with no new problem.' peer-ai doctor on next.18: 'Everything is set up correctly', with no problems and no warnings - where on next.16 it ended 'No problems, and 1 warning'. peer-ai check: 'Passed', every line a tick including '1 gap for mvp, each with a work item', where on next.16 it ended 'Passed, with 2 warnings'. Both improvements come from work already done rather than from the bump: the update warning cleared because the project is current, and the gap warning cleared because the threat model became ITEM-8.

'The project's ci:watch and ci:premerge scripts stay.' Both are untouched by this change - no file under scripts/ is in the diff - and the reason they are kept is recorded in the pull request rather than left implicit: Peer AI's gate is declared on pull_request against any base, but branch protection, which is what would make it mandatory, only ever guards main and is still off per issue #112. pre-merge-check.mjs refuses a draft, a non-open pull request and any check that is not a pass, naming the base branch when it is not main. The two do different jobs and neither replaces the other.

next.18's one behavioural change was seen working before it was trusted, on this very pull request: with #148 opened as a draft, 'gh pr checks 148' reports 'peer-ai check  skipping  0', where the same gate on #147 ran and reported 'pass' in 19s. So the draft condition fires, and the job is skipped rather than failing. The project's own guard was checked against that new state too: ci-status.mjs lists 'skipping' in SETTLED_BLOCKING_BUCKETS, so ci:premerge refuses to merge while the gate is skipped, which is the behaviour CLAUDE.md requires - a check that was skipped has not passed.

coverage.reason: No bug in this project's code was fixed. The defects fixed are in Peer AI itself, and what guards against regression is the exact version pin in four places plus the lockfile's integrity hashes.
No user journey is in scope. No file under apps/web/src or packages/core changed; the 487 tests are untouched and verify passed in CI on this commit.
No business rule changed. Nothing executable in the product is in the diff.
No test was added or changed.
No input boundary, route or permission in the product is in scope. The workflow's permissions were reviewed under SEC-28 in the infrastructure review and are unchanged.

coverage.evidence: What was checked is what ships: the gate CI runs is the committed peer-ai.yml, and the version it installs is the one written in that file. doctor and check were run from the same version this repository now names, so their output describes the committed state rather than a local one.

The edge case of adopting a release that skips drafts is that a project gate reading 'skipping' as green would open a hole; this project's does the opposite and refuses, which was checked in ci-status.mjs rather than assumed. The second edge case, two releases arriving at once, was handled by going to next.18 directly and reading both sets of notes, rather than applying next.17 and discovering next.18 afterwards.

summary: Pass, all four criteria on observed evidence. The one behavioural change was seen working on this pull request itself: the gate reports skipping on a draft, where it ran and passed on the last one. The project's own pre-merge guard already treats skipping as not passed, so the new behaviour opens no hole. doctor and check both end clean on next.18, where next.16 left warnings.
